preview: Abhishek Kalshetti shares his placement experience at Wells Fargo through an online assessment, a technical round, a senior leader interview, and an HR round, resulting in a job offer.
content: Abhishek Kalshetti B.Tech CE 2018-2022 Wells Fargo Eligibility: CGPA 6.75 and above Branches Allowed: CS, IT, EXTC, Electronics, Electrical, and Mechanical. Timeline and Events: Preplacement Talk: 8 August The test was conducted right after the pre-placement talk. Online Assessment: 1.Verbal 2.Business Aptitude 3.Coding Verbal: 12 questions in 15 mins based on detecting grammatical errors fill in the blanks and vocabulary. This was pretty easy if one has a moderate level of English knowledge. Business Aptitude: 15 questions in 25 mins. These were interpretation questions based on business graphs, candlesticks, etc. Coding: 2 questions in 60 minutes. 1.Array-based questions, about a game being played and rules, were given how this game is to be placed. I applied a brute force approach and was able to pass all the test cases. 2.Based on 2-D Array it was a variation of Minimum lines to cover all points. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/minimum-lines-cover-points/ I managed to pass 3 out of 11 test cases. Round 1:(Next Day--Technical Round) (We got the names of shortlisted students the same day.) Questions: 1.Interviewer first asked me to introduce myself. Keep this short and simple. Mention your internship in a line or two. Techstacks you’ve worked on, similarly mention your projects in a line or two. (Tip: Your introduction should sound very confident i.e your first impression is what will set the tone for further interview) 2.Interviewer asked a couple of questions about my internship. 3.Questions on ASP .NET Core (Since mentioned on my resume) 4.API Development in ASP .NET Core and follow-up questions about SQL Injection, dependency injection, and how are APIs platform-independent. 5.How I implemented my internship project in ASP .NET Core? 6.Then he asked me to explain my personal project. 7.Sum of diagonals of a given 2-D Array. 8.Difference between array and LinkedList. 9.Then the interviewer moved on to OOPS and CS Fundamentals Q’s. 10.What is OOPS and why was it introduced. 11.Types of inheritance. 12.What is a virtual function? 13.What is pure virtual function? 14.Difference between abstract class and interface. 15.Difference between private and protected access modifiers. 16.Then some OS questions. 17.What is a Page Fault? 18.Virtual Memory vs Segmentation. 19.Some questions on Deadlock. 20.What is Indexing? (DBMS) 21.Clustered Indexing vs Non-Clustered Indexing. 22.Explain different types of Joins. 23.Some SQL Queries. 24.Are API’s Platform Independent? (Yes, they are) 25.Then at last the interviewer asked me to explain my Flutter Project. The motivation behind the project. (Why did you build this project?) Do explain what is this project about. If you’ve used some resources/services like APIs do mention the source, how were these APIs playing role in your project? When you explain your project, do explain what kind of architecture you used for ex if you’ve used MVC(Model, View, Controller) mention that, and what did you use this.) Explain how did you break up your project into different modules and the approach used to implement them. For example, if you’ve used a specific package/library, mention how this library played a role in your project. Mostly important DRAW!! Keep drawing (MS Paint or anything), keep writing on a notepad for making the understanding clear. This helps a lot to you as well because you then can explain your points properly and the interviewer can also understand what you are trying to explain very easily. The interviewer was quite happy with my answers and asked me if I have any questions for him. Since the interviewer asked me a lot of questions about APIs and ASP .NET Core, I asked about the tech stacks he has worked on. He told me that, he had a lot of experience working with ASP .NET Core and API’s development using the same. Then we had a good discussion about APIs, how they are platform-independent, and the development of APIs using ASP .NET Core. As soon as my technical round got over I got an update for the second round. Round 2 (Senior Leader interview): The interviewer was very friendly, she asked me about my Round 1 Interview. Then she asked me to introduce myself. Then the interviewer asked me a puzzle. Pay an employee using a gold rod of 7 units? https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-4-pay-an-employee-using-a-gold-rod-of-7-units/ I gave the solution after some thinking. Then the interviewer confirmed that my answer was correct and now told me to code the solution. I was able to do this using a recursive approach. (Include/Not Include Method). The interviewer was satisfied with the solution. Then she moved on to my resume. Some questions about my internship. Difficulties faced while implementing the project. Explain the ML project mentioned in my resume. This interview lasted for 40 minutes. Round 3 (HR round): This was a telephonic round. Firstly the HR asked me to introduce myself. I gave a brief introduction about my academic background, mentioned my internship and the projects that I’ve worked on. The interviewer then asked me about my ML Project since the dataset used was the HR analysis of IBM. I explained to him in brief about the motivation behind the project and how the outcomes could be used. Then he asked me about my family background and if am comfortable with relocation (I said, Yes). And some more HR-type questions. This call lasted for around 20 Minutes. Results were announced at 8.05 PM,7 out of 31 were selected and I am happy to share that I was one of them. But on the same day, I got an offer from MSCI and I decided to go with MSCI. Tips: 1.Be calm, interviewers are generally helpful, keep explaining your approach step by step if you get stuck interviewer will give you hints use them, and complete your code. 2.You have to present your ideas/approaches very clearly. The interviewer must know what are you trying to do at each point. 3.You should know each and everything mentioned in your resume. That is you should be able to defend everything asked about your internships and projects.
